item.text: {"representations":[{"case_ref":"sample_634a74781104fc89","text":"Across March 30–April 12, sleep and steps dropped abruptly from the preceding 28-day baseline and stayed lower every day, including weekends, without recovery. Sleep averaged 331 versus 469 minutes (−138; −29%), with starts shifting from about 22:51 to 01:09 while waking remained 07:00. Steps averaged 2,643 versus 7,985 (−67%). Despite these concurrent declines, active minutes stayed near baseline (55 versus 54), in continuous bouts starting at 21:00. Low movement remained 451 versus 449 minutes, spread across ten roughly 45-minute daytime intervals separated by five-minute gaps. Resting heart rate rose slightly within its baseline range, from 55 initially to 56–57 bpm later (mean 56.3 versus 55.9); RMSSD remained 44.9 ms. Activity versus sleep ending the following day had a weak association (r=−0.15; 13 pairs), weaker than baseline (−0.36). The usual continuous 21:00 bouts shortened to 2–10 minutes when present; March 30 and April 8 recorded zero. Sleep remained near baseline: 469 versus 471 minutes, starts around 22:51, and waking consistently at 07:00. Low movement also stayed similar (448 versus 451 minutes), in ten daytime intervals with five-minute gaps. Resting heart rate remained 55–57 bpm (mean 56.3 versus 56.1); RMSSD averaged 44.8 versus 45.3 ms and increased modestly within the window. Their same-day association became moderately inverse (r=−0.59). Activity versus following-day sleep was modestly positive (r=0.32; 13 pairs), without establishing causation. Other measurements stayed near baseline: RMSSD 45.1 versus 44.8 ms, sleep 472 versus 471 minutes, steps 7,923 versus 7,938, active minutes 56 versus 55, and low movement 447 versus 450 minutes. All metrics were complete with adequate coverage."},{"case_ref":"sample_6afee74fd2861af0","text":"March 30–April 12 introduced a repeating weekday/weekend sleep pattern absent from the preceding 28-day baseline. Baseline sleep averaged 469 minutes in both groups, starting around 22:51 and ending at 07:00. All ten window weekdays averaged 390 minutes (−79), with starts at 00:07–00:14 and unchanged 07:00 waking. Both weekends, April 4–5 and 11–12, averaged 570 minutes (+101), starting at 01:05–01:15 and ending at 11:00. Shorter sleep returned April 6; the overall 441-minute mean and upward slope reflect this alternation rather than progressive recovery. Steps (7,939 versus 8,019), active minutes (55 versus 55), low movement (451 versus 451), resting heart rate (56.1 versus 56.5 bpm), and RMSSD (45.4 versus 45.3 ms) remained similar. Activity stayed in continuous 21:00 bouts; interrupted low movement began at 11:30 on weekends versus 10:00 weekdays. Activity versus following-day sleep was weakly associated (r=−0.15; 13 pairs). Coverage was adequate with no missing metrics."}]}
